comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch full-time 2026–2027 VU bachelor (RIO56003) is taught in the ACASA VU–UvA collaboration on the UvA campus. There are no formal specialisations. The adopted OER Articles11.1–11.4 establish ten compulsory6EC first-year units, thirteen compulsory6EC later units, a12EC thesis including colloquium and30EC genuine open study:180EC. The standard programme is used, not the shortened UvA-entry pathway or pre2017 transition. Comedy is an optional additional6EC module, as the visible Appendix4 footnote confirms, despite appearing unqualified on recruitment pages; it is not added to the compulsory total. Article9.1 requires a positive BSA for post-first-year assessment, subject to catalogue conditions; thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. Article14.1 normally requires48first-yearEC for a positive full-time BSA. Article10.4 requires a Dutch diagnostic test and, on failure, the remedial course, outside180EC. Article11.5 requires85% attendance for Historical Sources, Philosophy of the Humanities, ACASA Excursion and Reception/Creative Writing, otherwise repeat or an additional assignment. Article12.1 allows a minor, electives, study abroad or up to12EC internship; outside VU/UvA needs examination-board approval. Normally at most12EC introductory study, exceptionally24EC for specified VU/UvA minors or one-language acquisition packages; foreign language-improvement courses outside an academic degree do not qualify. Minor course prerequisites still apply. Optional honours are additional, not part of180EC. Thesis is disciplinary research; Article3.10 guarantees draft feedback under the thesis regulation. Programme tutoring occurs at least twice per year (Article7.3).

exception.reason: UCR offers genuine study of ancient myth, Greek archaeology and democratic heritage, rhetoric, literary interpretation and philosophy. The strongest existing24-course programme nevertheless devotes most of its curriculum to general literary/communication methods, modern history, modern media, Renaissance art and general social research. It does not establish the defining integrated progression in Greek and Latin philology: sustained interpretation of difficult original texts using grammar/commentary, linguistic analysis of both languages, specialised epic/tragedy/lyric, post-classical Greek/Latin transmission and independent classical literary or linguistic research. World Myth & Literature explicitly includes Homer, Virgil and Byzantine romance in a global comparative frame; that substantial contribution is preserved, but it is not the specialist philological sequence. Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy provide a strong material/political case, not a substitute for the textual discipline. The second programme adds extensive modern law/EU/international politics; the stated ancient-to-modern migration question does not make those courses training in Roman evidence. Stylistics, generic adaptation and art historiography do not supply historical grammar, classical reception research or philological methods merely by adjacency. A focused reconstruction from the whole workbook retains these useful contributions but finds no further specialist classical-text progression to remedy the programme-level shortfall. No defensible complete UCR response is established. This conclusion is not based solely on missing language teaching, a degree title, a matching quota or teacher licensing.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Greek and Latin Languages and Cultures combines advanced reading and interpretation of Greek and Latin texts with linguistics, literature, ancient cultural history, philosophy and the later reception of antiquity. Students progress from language and textual foundations to specialist study and independent classical research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers valuable study of ancient myth, Greek archaeology and democratic heritage, rhetoric, philosophy and literary interpretation. These contributions do not form a complete programme centred on the sustained philological study of Greek and Latin texts, their linguistic structures and their transmission. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC pathway comprises 60 EC of first-year study, 78 EC of later compulsory courses, a 12 EC thesis including colloquium and 30 EC of open study. Comedy is an optional additional module. Thesis entry requires all first- and second-year courses. The Dutch diagnostic or remedial language requirement adds no credits; specified practical courses require 85% attendance.
